Check a bundle and the R that will fit it, before anything is submitted

Source: R/hpc.R
check_hpc_bundle.Rd

Checks a bundle written by write_hpc_bundle(), where it is to be run: on the login node of the cluster, from the bundle's script check.sh, which loads R as the bundle's settings say and calls this function. It takes seconds, fits nothing and installs nothing.

Usage

check_hpc_bundle(dir = ".")

Arguments

dir

A character string, the folder of the bundle. Defaults to the working folder, which is where check.sh runs it.

Value

TRUE, invisibly, when every check passes. A message lists what was checked.

Details

It checks, in order, that the files of the bundle are all there and unchanged since they were written (by their checksums, so a copy that was cut short or a file edited by hand is found); that the installed rTFT is the version that wrote the bundle; that cmdstanr is installed and finds CmdStan; and that every model of the bundle can be assembled on its data. The first problem stops the check, with an error that says what to do about it.

The version is compared by its number and, when both the rTFT that wrote the bundle and the one installed came from GitHub, by the commit each was installed from, since copies of a development version share a number and can differ in their code. A copy installed from a folder on your own machine has no commit to compare, so for it only the number is checked. run_hpc_task() makes the same check at the start of each task, since the library can change while tasks wait in the queue.

See also

write_hpc_bundle(), which writes the bundle.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# on the cluster, from the folder of the bundle; check.sh runs the same
check_hpc_bundle()
} # }
